To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

collaboration is an effective means for individuals with low levels or understanding of a domain to improve their understanding but only if the partner has only moderately higher understanding of the domain.
collaboration is effective in domains that are conceptually complex, but only if the collaborators have similar conceptions of the causal structure of the domain.

(a) collaboration in domains characterized with conceptual change is possible and (b) collaboration is more productive when it is asymmetric, in that individuals with lower levels of understanding benefit from it more than individuals with higher levels of understanding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of learning and teaching.
the question of how to promote conceptual change in the context of collaboration.
how people learn to think scientifically.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of the study suggest that collaboration is an effective means of science learning, but only for individuals who are less knowledgeable about the topic of discussion.
collaboration in domains that require conceptual change is effective, but that the learning from such collaboration depends on the initial levels of understanding of the collaborators.

the collaboration in domains characterized with conceptual change can be possible and the learning from such collaboration can be asymmetric and unequal, and thus, bridging the conceptual divide requires instruction more aligned with novices than with experts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peer collaboration can facilitate learning in science, but that the nature of that collaboration is dependent on the nature of the domain.
the collaboration is effective, but it is effective only for those who need it most.

collaboration can be an effective means for learning, but that it can be more or less effective for learners with different starting levels of understanding, and that this effectiveness is dependent on the level of the partner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of collaborative learning activities should be informed by the learners’ initial understanding of the domain.
collaboration can be an effective means of conceptual change, but only under certain conditions.
collaboration can be an effective learning tool for individuals who are not experts in a given domain.
